_readme: Ground truth for the loudness chain. Generated by scripts/make-fixtures.sh,
measured by scripts/verify-fixtures.ts, asserted hermetically by
`source` is the field that earns its keep. An `arithmetic` value follows from
ITU-R BS.1770 and a measurement disagreeing with it means the chain is wrong.
A `frozen` value is only what ffmpeg said on the day, and a disagreement means
a dependency moved. Collapsing the two into one bag of constants is how a
fixture corpus quietly turns back into a thing that agrees with itself.
The .wav files are NOT committed — they are ~35 MB and regenerate

asserts: K-weighting at 1 kHz (+0.6977 dB) cancels the BS.1770 offset (-0.691 dB) to within 0.007 dB
two identical channels sum to +3.01 dB over one, so a STEREO 1 kHz sine reads integrated == peak dBFS
identical peak to the stereo tone but exactly 3.01 LU quieter — this is the control that proves the stereo anchor measures channel summation and not a coincidence
linear gain to -14 LUFS lands the peak at about -1.35 dBTP, under the -1 ceiling, so nothing forces compression
LRA is deliberately 6 LU rather than 0 — see the LRA=0.00 trap; a flat file can never report linear
four steps at 0/-6/-12/-18 dB all sit inside the -20 LU relative gate, giving LRA 18 LU
linear gain to -14 LUFS would put the peak at -0.20 dBTP, above the ceiling, so loudnorm falls back and compresses
take-screen's predictedLinearOutputPeak must reach the same conclusion ffmpeg did — the end-to-end check on the forces-dynamic rule
a tone at fs/4 offset 45 degrees lands every sample on 0.7071 x A while the waveform peaks at A — a derivable +3.01 dB gap

ffmpeg reads this about +0.5 dB HIGH against both the arithmetic and an independent 64x resampler, hence the wide true-peak tolerance; the durable assertion is the structural one, that true peak exceeds sample peak by roughly 3 dB
integrated loudness lands near +3 LUFS because K-weighting boosts 11 kHz, which puts it outside loudnorm's measured_I range entirely — this fixture measures peaks, not loudness
